legend: Consider all equalities of form a+b=c%%ZSMJ0%%, where a%%ZSMJ1%% has A%%ZSMJ2%% digits, b%%ZSMJ3%% has B%%ZSMJ4%% digits, and c%%ZSMJ5%% has C%%ZSMJ6%% digits. All the numbers are positive integers and are written without leading zeroes. Find the k%%ZSMJ7%%-th lexicographically smallest equality when written as a string like above or determine that it does not exist.
For example, the first three equalities satisfying A=1%%ZSMJ8%%, B=1%%ZSMJ9%%, C=2%%ZSMJ10%% are
An equality s%%ZSMJ14%% is lexicographically smaller than an equality t%%ZSMJ15%% with the same lengths of the numbers if and only if the following holds:
in the first position where s%%ZSMJ16%% and t%%ZSMJ17%% differ, the equality s%%ZSMJ18%% has a smaller digit than the corresponding digit in t%%ZSMJ19%%.
input: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line of input contains a single integer t%%ZSMJ20%% (1≤t≤103%%ZSMJ21%%) — the number of test cases. The description of test cases follows.
The first line of each test case contains integers A%%ZSMJ22%%, B%%ZSMJ23%%, C%%ZSMJ24%%, k%%ZSMJ25%% (1≤A,B,C≤6%%ZSMJ26%%, 1≤k≤1012%%ZSMJ27%%).
Each input file has at most 5%%ZSMJ28%% test cases which do not satisfy A,B,C≤3%%ZSMJ29%%.
output: For each test case, if there are strictly less than k%%ZSMJ30%% valid equalities, output −1%%ZSMJ31%%.
Otherwise, output the k%%ZSMJ32%%-th equality as a string of form a+b=c%%ZSMJ33%%.
note: Int the third test case, there are no solutions as the smallest possible values for a%%ZSMJ36%% and b%%ZSMJ37%% are larger than the maximal possible value of c%%ZSMJ38%% — 10+10=20>9%%ZSMJ39%%.
Please note that whitespaces in the output matter.
